bullets.title: AMZN: AWS guides 40%+ growth in 2027-28; stock -7% on Q4 OI guide miss
bullets.body: AWS grew 39.3% YoY to $45.98B (beat vs $44.9B consensus) but missed ~43% buyside expectations; management guided 40%+ AWS growth explicitly for both 2027 and 2028, first time Amazon has projected specific future-year guidance. AWS backlog surged $82B QoQ to $578B; 2028 AWS at 40% CAGR implies ~$342B, ~$20B above Street. Q4 OI guide midpoint $31.0B was 6.6% below consensus, driving stock down ~7% pre-market. North America operating margin expanded 320bps YoY to 7.7%. Hedgeye and Citi both maintain Buy/$350 PT; Citi's Josey raises OI estimates 2%/10% for 27E/28E.

bullets.title: INTC: -26% on PC weakness; multiple downgrades, PT cuts to $70
bullets.body: Intel crashed 25.8% pre-market after a significant miss in Client Computing Group; 2H26 PC unit volumes declining ~25% YoY and server segment supply-constrained. Roth Capital downgraded to Neutral from Buy, cutting PT to $70 from $120 (24% downside). DA Davidson cut PT to $70 from $100, maintaining Neutral, citing weak PC demand and memory cost pressure. 2027 Diamond Rapids roadmap compromised by SMT removal; earliest leadership opportunity now 2028 Coral Rapids. Capex remains ~$20B in 2026 with strong increases expected in 2027.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Search miss triggers -12.6% T+1 decline; AI monetization concerns rise
bullets.body: Alphabet's Search revenue growth slowed to +12% YoY from +17%, missing expectations on FX, softer retail/media spend, and lower AI Mode monetization — largest T+1 earnings decline on record at -12.6%. Google Cloud grew 103% with $561B backlog (includes $16.8B Crux AI TPU deal); Gemini 4 Carbon ranks first on AA Intelligence Index with widest lead over open models. Hedgeye's McCullough explicitly reaffirmed a short on GOOGL, citing slowing core business and Quad 4 concerns. KeyBanc also flags negative read-through from Search miss to Apple Services via TAC correlation.

bullets.title: RDDT: -23.5% on earnings; Citi cuts PT to $186 on GOOGL traffic headwinds
bullets.body: Reddit fell 23.5% pre-market; DAU growth falling low-double-digits in Q4, ads 6% below expectations, and ad revenue +54% YoY with 54% incremental margins but declining GOOGL Search referral traffic is the core concern. Citi maintained Buy but cut PT to $186 from $245, reducing revenue/EBITDA estimates -2%/-4% in 27E and -4%/-5% in 28E. DA Davidson kept Neutral. Click volumes +50%+ YoY and conversion volumes +3x+ YoY remain positives but insufficient to offset user growth deceleration.

bullets.title: MSFT: Azure +48%, guides +49-50%; capex trimmed to ~$170B
bullets.body: Microsoft beat and raised on Azure strength (+48% YoY, guiding +49-50%); commercial RPO hit $677B. Capex lowered to ~$170B from ~$175B on third-party delays; GOOGL and AMZN left 2026 guidance unchanged but signal higher 2027 spend. Agent 365 registry at 50M+ agents (+30% QoQ); Copilot daily users up ~50% QoQ. Open-source model revenue on Foundry rose 10x. Stock pressured post-earnings on $25B+ debt sale despite operational strength.

bullets.title: META: Beat + raised on AI tailwinds; raised ~$100B in capital
bullets.body: Meta beat and raised consensus estimates driven by AI advertising tailwinds, and raised approximately $100B in capital. Broadcom launched a $63B custom-chip SPV to ease AI funding concerns. No specific PT changes in these items, but Meta flagged as bullish alongside hyperscaler AI capex buildout; 2027 consensus capex implies +59% step-up from Q3 run rates — the largest among Mag 7.

bullets.title: RBLX: -13.8% on Q4 bookings guide -10% to -15% YoY; GTA VI risk
bullets.body: Roblox fell 13.8% pre-market; Q3 beat but Q4 bookings guidance assumes YoY decline of 10-15%, with delayed reacceleration and age verification headwinds. DA Davidson maintained Neutral. GTA VI release on 11/19 creates additional unknown competitive pressure on engagement.

bullets.title: DELL, HPQ hit by INTC PC miss; DELL at 52-week low -8-12%
bullets.body: DELL fell 8.2-11.9% and HPQ fell 9.7% in sympathy with Intel's PC segment miss, as rising costs, prices, and inventory weigh on PC demand. DELL also hit a 52-week low on the Canadian exchange. AMD down 9.4% in broader semi selloff (SOXX -7%).

bullets.title: MRVL/LITE: All-stock deal reportedly imminent at modest premium
bullets.body: Marvell Technology is in advanced talks to acquire Lumentum Holdings in an all-stock deal at 'not all that large a premium,' per CNBC's David Faber; announcement could come as soon as next week. LITE rose ~9% after-hours to $999.15; MRVL fell 6.4% to $235.20 on the news.

bullets.title: SNDK: Data Center revenue +61% QoQ; NAND sold out despite Kioxia miss
bullets.body: SanDisk beat estimates with Data Center revenue +61% QoQ and NAND described as sold out; 60-90GB NAND per CPU required in agentic workloads is a key demand driver. However SNDK fell 8.8% pre-market in sympathy with Kioxia's Dec Q guidance miss (14-16% below consensus) and broader memory/semi weakness. Kioxia's ASP growth collapsed to 3-4% QoQ from ~30% prior quarter; Hedgeye remains short the memory complex.

bullets.title: COHR: MS cuts PT to $325 on limited near-term margin catalysts
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reduced COHR price target from $375 to $325, maintaining Equal-weight. Gross margin improvement from 6-inch substrate ramp expected to be modest near-term (~20bps step-up in FQ2). Buyside expects ~$2.38bn revenue and ~40.8% GM for F1Q27 vs consensus $2.31bn/40.6% GM. Industry demand continues to outpace supply with favorable pricing into 2027-28; InP supply constraints reinforced by AXTI commentary.

bullets.title: DLR: Citi raises PT to $234; record bookings, double-digit core FFO growth
bullets.body: Citi's Mike Rollins raised Digital Realty PT to $234 from $226 after record bookings and accelerating revenue growth; management increased guidance and expects ~1.5GW available capacity by end-2028. DLR beat on 0-1 MW bookings at $152M, raised core FFO/share guidance, and MS TMT flagged DLR as beating buyside expectations on hyperscale leasing. Analyst expects double-digit core FFOPS growth for next few years.

bullets.title: AAPL: KeyBanc Underweight at $250; iPhone Duo cracks, Services headwinds
bullets.body: KeyBanc rates Apple Underweight at $250 PT, citing iPhone Duo foldable cracked inner display complaints likely to drive cancellations, US carrier upgrade rates down 9.9% YoY in Q3, and negative read-through from GOOGL Search miss to Apple Services (TAC correlation). Mac consensus estimates of 6.7M/6.9M units viewed as too high with PC shipments down mid-teens. Apple also reducing App Store commission to 26% from 30% in Taiwan. AAPL reports next week.

bullets.title: FSLR: MS cuts PT to $307; GLJ downgrades to Hold at $161 on booking delays
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reduced FSLR PT to $307 from $326 (remaining Overweight) as customers delay 2028-29 shipment bookings amid tariff/inflation headwinds on project economics; analyst expects acceleration in bookings and pricing in 1H27 with path to ~$16/sh EPS in 2029. GLJ Research separately downgraded to Hold from Buy with $161 PT (9% downside vs $177), a wide gap to FactSet consensus of $259.67.

bullets.title: INTC/PINS/RBLX: DA Davidson notable TMT color post-earnings
bullets.body: DA Davidson flagged INTC Neutral at $70 PT (down from $100) on Client Computing weakness; expects INTC Renewal Deal with PDFS to scale to $100M+/yr. PINS disappointed in Q3 on EU Cross Border headwinds but posted 12th consecutive quarter of LDD MAU growth; recovery expected to accelerate in 2027 as EU challenges ease. RBLX neutral on conservative Q4 guide despite Q3 beat.

bullets.title: DASH: Acquires Instacart (CART) for ~$17B; core orders +17% YoY
bullets.body: DoorDash agreed to acquire Instacart for approximately $17B; Citi maintains Buy with $255 PT. Core restaurant orders grew +17% YoY, US restaurant orders accelerating, and DashPass reached an all-time high. Citi analyst views the deal constructively given grocery flywheel potential.

bullets.title: TTD: Raymond James cautious into 3Q adtech cycle on competitive pressures
bullets.body: Raymond James published 3Q26 adtech preview favoring Unity (U), PubMatic (PUBM), MNTN, and Viant for CTV/political tailwinds while remaining cautious on The Trade Desk where competitive pressures constrain recovery. Political advertising expected to provide meaningful Q4 tailwind. Mobile advertising healthy except in gaming.

bullets.title: SPOT: AI Remix tier potentially launching early 2027 at Grammy Awards for $4-5/mo
bullets.body: Citi reports Spotify is planning an AI Remix subscription tier launch in early 2027, potentially timed to the Grammy Awards in February, at an additional $4-5/month charge. Deals have reportedly been struck with UMG, Merlin, and Believe. This represents a new monetization vector above existing premium tiers.

bullets.title: APP, OKLO, QBTS hit 52-week lows; broad small-cap/speculative flush
bullets.body: APP fell to a 52-week low (down 5.5% today, -61.9% YTD) after Edgewater Research downgrade; OKLO hit 52-week low (-6.6% today, -82.5% YTD); QBTS at 52-week low (-5.8% today, -68.2% YTD). Broader market down 1.5% with VIX +13.2% to 19.47; MS QDS flagged $28bn levered ETF selling as 8th largest on record, plus $3-6bn pension and $10bn macro systematic selling.

bullets.title: LYV: Citi maintains Buy at $212; FTC case heads to trial after motion-to-dismiss denial
bullets.body: Judge Frimpong denied Live Nation's motion to dismiss the FTC BOTS Act/Section 5 case on September 28, 2026, sending it into discovery. Citi views the case as not particularly strong — TradeDesk was shuttered and all-in pricing now compliant with May 2025 FTC rule — but trial risk adds incremental uncertainty. Citi PT $212 at ~17x 2028E EV-AOI.
